title: Wunan Foundation: Breaking the Cycle
author: Aaron
body:
The Wunan Foundation works to give the Aboriginal people of the East Kimberley access to the opportunities they need to live independent and fulfilling lives. Wunan uses the metaphor of swimming the river to illustrate the challenges faced by Aboriginal people as they navigate their way to employment and housing via the education system.

Historically, one of the biggest obstacles to accessing these opportunities has been a general lack of expectation from successive governments, as well as the wider community. This has led to Aboriginal people becoming stuck in the welfare trap, with many also developing a dependence on alcohol and drugs. Domestic violence, mental illness and suicide have also proven depressing outcomes, arising all too often from this cycle of disadvantage.

It’s estimated that around 60 per cent of children in the region miss the necessary parental support to obtain the opportunities that would break this cycle. It’s these children who now benefit from Wunan’s specialised programs.

Through their Pathway to Home Ownership program, Wunan assists those looking to buy or build a home, while also providing skills in financial literacy. Support is also given to people wishing to access Kununurra’s public housing via the Move to Town initiative, while the Financial Capability Hub helps Aboriginal people to develop their overall money management skills.

The Parent & Community Engagement program encourages parents to engage with their child’s school and support their learning at home. Driver Training Programs in Kununurra and Halls Creek provide the skills needed to assist Aboriginal people to obtain employment. Wunan also operates a medical practice, a business support service and even a wholly Aboriginal-owned and operated Bed and Breakfast.

The challenges the Wunan Foundation is helping Aboriginal people to overcome are summarised in the short video ‘Swimming the River’, narrated by Wunan’s Chairman, Ian Trust. You can watch the video here:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0P9FRacTji0

The APT Foundation was grateful for the time Wunan’s Eddy Gaskill, Amanda Fernando and Dr Stephanie Trust recently gave. Their online visit offered the APT Foundation and the wider APT Travel Group family further insight into the nature of the problems, solutions and opportunities being worked through on a daily basis in the East Kimberley.
